steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Ugh...

Your vision blurs as darkness surges from all sides, accompanied by an overwhelming floral fragrance that seeps into your core and drains your vigor. Your knees buckle, and with your last shred of consciousness, you only manage to adjust your posture to protect your head from the impending fall.
But instead of collapsing helplessly onto the spirit-infested street as expected, you feel an ice-cold hand through your clothes steady your back, deftly halting your fall.
That day... merit... too greedy... futile... thankfully...

You feel yourself being propped up against something. A fragmented voice drifts down from above, the words too indistinct to grasp, and something warm flows into your mouth. You can't tell what it is, but the overpowering darkness that had enveloped you begins to soften.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...! Did I... pass out from exhaustion? I knew there was something wrong with this street...

Your consciousness snaps back, and your eyes fly open. Years of experience kick in as you immediately check your limbs for freedom of movement and assess your mental clarity. Only after confirming everything is in order do you cautiously survey your surroundings.
The medicine has barely reached your stomach, and the needles are still in place. My friend, for your own well-being, please remain still and composed for a while longer.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You're... the one who warned me on the street earlier? Did you save me from those "spirits"?

The young girl emerges silently from the shadows, responding with both a nod and a shake of her head. Her unnervingly serene demeanor remains unchanged as she peers at you through her heavy bangs with clear eyes, delicate acupuncture needles held between her fingers.
Yes. You may call me Wuhuanzi. But... I am but a wandering herbalist from Eastia, traveling across lands to save lives and accumulate merit. I can't slay demons or exorcise evil spirits.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But you clearly warned me not to linger here... Doesn't that mean you have already noticed something wrong with this place?

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: I merely noticed the ominous shadows surrounding you, signs of vital energy depletion, so I thought to offer a word of caution, hoping to gain some small merit. Had you heeded my warning and turned back then, the situation wouldn't have become so grave.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Yet now, you have glimpsed the forbidden and treaded paths you ought not to have. Your Qi lay scattered... This is why I resorted to such measures—brewing a decoction of eighty-one herbs and applying gold needles to your acupoints—to pull you back from the brink.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Let this serve as a lesson, at least. You must now understand that your constitution cannot withstand the forces at work here. Any further struggle would be futile. You would do well to leave this place of turmoil while you can.

Though her words remain somewhat cryptic, you flex your palm—still pierced with needles—and find your strength has indeed returned. The mysterious decoction she administered radiates warmth in your stomach, its contents unknown yet undeniably potent.

...Could this be the mysterious power of Eastia? You can't help but feel a deep sense of reverence. The young herbalist before you may be peculiar in her demeanor, but she has genuinely helped you—surely not one of those spirits coveting your "Qi."
In that case... you decide to take the risk.

options: I wish I could leave, but there's something I must do first.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Many others have been drawn into this fete full of strange spirits—both my friends and innocent DisCity people. Their physical bodies, existing beyond this "story," are growing weaker by the moment.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: And that's probably because everyone's vital energy—or Qi—as you mentioned, is being drained—by the spirits, and by the wisteria. If this continues...

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: I see. But this fete harbors unfathomable dangers. In your condition... how do you intend to resolve this? You'll likely collapse again within a few hours.
Her amber eyes fix upon you with an intent gaze, as calm and steady as her voice. Faced with her sobering yet precise question, you take a deep breath.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You're right, I won't last long. So I was wondering... would you be willing to help restore that "Qi" of mine regularly?

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: You're asking me... just to restore your Qi?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Yes. You've already saved me once, haven't you? I figure with effective treatments, I can explore more areas and find clues to resolve this fete situation. I don't mind falling down... as long as I can get back up again.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Qi isn't like medicine that you can simply replenish after it's depleted. Repeated treatments won't be very effective, and I can't guarantee they'll be painless or harmless... It's an inefficient and taxing solution.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: An inefficient solution will do. As long as it works... and as long as you're willing to help. I apologize, I know this is a presumptuous request, but there are people I must save, things I must do. I really need your help.
You meet the young Eastian herbalist's scrutinizing gaze with unwavering sincerity. After a moment, Wuhuanzi is the first to avert her gaze.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: ...Is this what they mean by "ignorance is bliss"? ...Very well, I suppose rescuing such a headstrong and audacious soul could be deemed a form of merit.

Muttering to herself, Wuhuanzi bends down to gather her belongings. You watch her movements nervously, only to find that after packing up, all she does is take a single small step to your side, bundle on her back, and plant herself firmly there.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Does this mean you agree? Are you... coming with me?

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Naturally. A patient lacking self-care awareness requires constant supervision, and I cannot afford to forgo such a chance for merit... Besides, following you should lead to many people in need of treatment—plenty of good deeds to accumulate merit, I dare say.

A burden lifts from your chest now that the concern of "Qi" limitations no longer haunts you. Gathering your strength, you stride forward, and the clear jingling of ornaments trails closely behind like a shadow. A smile unconsciously graces your lips.
